steps.content: The FAC's vehicle looks even fancier than customized cargo trucks. This is no doubt the result of Vautour Bleu's regular "contributions" to the officials. The big shots in DisCity clearly want no harm to come to her.
Once inside, Vautour Bleu helps herself to a cocktail from the fridge, which is clearly not a regular item in an FAC vehicle. She settles down to enjoy the drink with perfect composure.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: As per our superiors' orders, we won't restrict your movements. However, we strongly advise that you remain sober until the investigation officially begins.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: We wouldn't want you to be so intoxicated that you'll conveniently forget the true identity of Lyman, that Outland infiltrator, before the questioning even begins.
The FAC soldier sitting across from Vautour Bleu speaks stiltedly, his tone and gaze vigilant and hostile. To him, she's clearly nothing more than a common criminal disturbing the city' order.
But these low-ranking soldiers' standoffish attitude fails to intimidate Vautour Bleu a bit. She lounges in the leather seat languidly, playfully swirling her glass at the soldier.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Easy, young man, this level of hospitality won't cloud my judgment. Besides... I'm already here to honor our arrangement. Relax, your boss won't be disappointed.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: But what about you all... This can't be an easy assignment, can it? You get no supplies out here in WhiteSands, only annoying desert bandits and disasters. And you have to sit here ramrod straight for days on end... Isn't it exhausting?

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: That's none of your concern. The FAC is well-stocked with Hypercubes. We've never feared desert bandits or disasters.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Besides, we've deployed top-tier equipment to expedite your transit to DisCity. In no more than three days, you'll be handed over to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Oh? So I'm an important witness, aren't I? Am I in the VIP lounge now? Haha.
Vautour Bleu lets out a derisive laugh.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: How very fitting of the mighty DisCity.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Back then, it took me three whole years to trek this same journey...
Western WhiteSands, Territory of House Noailles

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen, I have sorrowful news to announce.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Three months ago, we lost contact with my husband Alden Noailles and my son Joel. We've been trying to find their whereabouts since then, but to no avail.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Worse still, the suspension of our business during these three months has placed us in severe financial difficulty.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Two months ago, defending against the disaster depleted most of our Hypercube reserves. Yesterday, a new disaster began looming and is now approaching us. We... I must face reality.
Her voice trembled before she can even finish, dissolving into quiet sobs.
Most of the caravan's core members had joined that trading expedition three months ago, and none had been heard from since. Losing so many elite members at once left the family's caravan leaderless.

Now, the remaining members and relatives were overwhelmed by the profound grief of losing their family, friends, and leaders, as well as anxiety about their future. The disasters, the Hypercubes, the fate of their caravan...

steps.speaker: Emma
steps.content: What... what do we do now? Will our family split? I don't want that...

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Nonsense! Whoever wants to leave may go ahead. I'm staying right here with the lady and the family!

steps.speaker: Emma
steps.content: Me too! ...But even if we stay, can we really protect them? We're almost out of Hypercubes...

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Why don't we go to DisCity? It's the largest city there is. There's bound to be plenty of business there! We could set up a new trade route and start fresh together.

steps.speaker: Landon
steps.content: Easy for you to say! DisCity is on the other side of WhiteSands! Who's gonna lead us? The master and young master are both missing. Who else could guide us through?
The room fell in awkward silence. A name lied on everyone's tip of tongue, but no one had the heart to speak out.
Lady Madeleine, the eldest daughter of the Noailles. A natural-born businesswoman whose talent surpassed her brother's, she had already been handling multi-million contracts while still in her teens.

Yet she had never been into it. A lover of art, fine cuisine, flowers, and the pleasures of life, she had declined the offer to lead the caravan many times before. Could they really ask her to shoulder such a heavy burden that would overwhelm even the best leader?
Outside the door, the girl pressed her forehead against the wood, listening to the family servants volunteering to share the burden of leadership. She clenched her fists, then slowly relaxed them.

In the shadow of the ornately carved door, a symbol of her family's glory, the girl composed herself, carefully arranging her face until it mirrored her father and brother's casual optimism. Then she pushed the door open, determinedly.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Everyone, enough. I will take it over. I will lead everyone to DisCity.

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: Madeleine...! Are you sure about this? Don't push yourself. Once I'm old enough, I could also lead us to DisCity!

steps.speaker: Landon
steps.content: That's right, Miss. We're an old and useless lot, but we can still...

Madeleine raised her hand to silence the words from her servants. Seeing the mixture of concern, hope, and disbelief in their eyes, she adopted a more serious tone and her expression grew more resolute.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: I mean every word I said. It's settled. Though I can't guarantee success in leading all of us across WhiteSands, I can never be so heartless as to leave you all here to die.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Now, let me assign our jobs. Emma, Landon, take inventory of all sellable goods and pack them up. Make sure our packs are as neatly as possible.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Hugh, I know you have a copy of the map that Father and Brother carried with them. Bring it to me tomorrow morning.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Yes, yes, of course! At your word, Miss!
As she gave one order after another, the reception room grew lively again. Not only were those called upon bubbling with excitement, but the rest all began picturing a future.

steps.speaker: Servant A
steps.content: I've heard DisCity is the largest Hypercube producer, and the safest city too! Once we get there, all our troubles will be behind us!

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: True, but to reach DisCity safely, we must plan our route as carefully as possible. We have a long journey ahead.

steps.speaker: Servant B
steps.content: Have we got enough supplies for the trip? We can always trade along the way! That's what we do best. Come on everyone, let's show them what we're made of!

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Yes, that's definitely our strength. I'll plan our route based on our inventory, and if we work together as one, we will reach DisCity.
Seeing how her attitude and words successfully dispelled the gloom hanging over the room, Madeleine secretly let out a sigh of relief.

At last, she knew her strategy worked. Just as her vision of the future ignited hope in their eyes, their renewed spirit and optimism now shone like an oasis in the boundless deserts, showing her the way forward.
Hope and dreams would guide them to the promised land. That will be the day. That must be the day.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Um, Miss... Have you thought about, well, using a different name?

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Why? Is something wrong with my name?

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: The merchant caravans in WhiteSands are all roughnecks like me. Your name... may sound too soft for other traders to take you seriously. And better not go by Noailles either. We don't want those debt collectors coming after us.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: ...Then how about, Vautour Bleu.
The girl's gaze rested quietly on her half-finished desert landscape. Paints were a luxury in their harsh journey, so she could only mix whatever colors she had left for the painting.
A vulture, against the blue sky, gorging itself on a corpse in the sand.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Vautour Bleu... A blue vulture! What a majestic name! Those desert bandits won't even dare come near you!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Have you heard about Vautour Bleu? That lady boss is really something, young but ruthless. Her people burned down every single one of Red Claw's depots when their talk didn't go well. Didn't leave them a single straw.

steps.speaker: Drunk Patron
steps.content: Now everyone around here has to go through her for goods. She's good, way too ******* good at this.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: More than that. Do you know how much her caravan makes in a single run? At least this much. And you know what's the real shit about her?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: While others have no choice but to surrender their goods to desert bandits, she's found a way to trade with them! Good thing her caravan is still small. Otherwise, she's prolly gonna take over the whole WhiteSands!

steps.speaker: Drunk Patron
steps.content: No shit. No matter how big her business is, when disasters strike, everyone's got to run and hide. No one can stand that.

steps.speaker: Drunk Patron
steps.content: Look at the Noailles. They were basically on the throne just a few years ag—Ow! Who the hell hit me...

steps.speaker: Landon
steps.content: Miss, the sandstorm is gaining on us. We have three hours at most! Even if we run now, I'm afraid half of the caravan won't make it!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Get the supply trucks over here. We don't have enough Hypercubes left to protect all vehicles, prioritize these ones and our crew. As for the cargo, save what we can and leave the rest.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Miss, but these goods are everything we have! If we lose them, we'll have to start over again from scratch!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Don't be silly. I will never choose some cargo over you guys' lives!
But Vautour Bleu's stern words couldn't stop the stubborn old servant.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: We still have some Hypercubes left on the trucks. I've checked. Get two of our best drivers to take the trucks west, and we'll be able to slip past the storm's flank!

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: We'll regroup at the next stop after the storm passes! If we can save these goods, we can rebuild everything!

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: I've spent my whole life behind the wheel dodging disasters like this. Today's the day I show the storm what I've got.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: This isn't just some ordinary sandstorm! Hugh, you can't throw your life away! Hugh—!

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: Miss, me and the boys found a mining site. Looks like it's covered by quicksand, but we're thinking of checking it out.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: No. You can't go.

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: Madeleine! I know you're worried about everyone after what happened to Hugh, but we can't keep going on like this!

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: We're already running low on goods, and even you can't conjure merchandise out of thin air! If we secure that mining site, we'll have a new source of supply!

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: Even if it's not a Hypercube mine, any mineral vein we find would make our days so much easier.

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: I'll just take a quick look! I promise I'll come back in one piece!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...He never came back. It wasn't until that moment that I truly understood how desire leads us all to our doom.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Madeleine... Don't... don't blame your brother. He just so wanted to be a grown man.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...I know, I just can't... keep going, Mom.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Madeleine, oh, Madeleine...! My dear daughter...
A headstone carved from sand and stone marked this crude grave.
Leaving her mother's favorite flowers from homeland, Vautour Bleu gathered a handful of sand and slowly poured it onto the gravestone.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Landon, how many of us left?

steps.speaker: Landon
steps.content: Thirty.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Hah... We started out with fifty. Lost almost half of us in such a short time.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Was it worth it? All of this just for a few crates of goods and some useless minerals!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Answer me, Landon! Was it worth it?!
She lashed out uncharacteristically before her mother's grave, her old servant silently accompanying her aside. Tears running dry, she regained her composure, rising once again from the ground.
The sunset bled crimson across the sky.

No one called her Madeleine anymore. Lady Noailles, sister, daughter... One by one, her old identities have faded away. Now, she stands as Vautour Bleu and Vautour Bleu only, who devours everything, including the remains of her enemies.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...Let's go. We can't delay any longer. We must reach DisCity as quickly as possible, whatever the cost.

At last, after two years and two hundred eighty-seven days, with more than half of the crew gone, bereft of all families and her most trusted staff, Vautour Bleu led the remaining crew to DisCity's border.
Around the evening bonfire, an unusual silence fell over the camp. Their eyes fixed upon the towering city walls in the distance almost reverently, each mind painting pictures of what lay beyond.
Vautour Bleu negotiated with DisCity's border officials, securing the precious entry permits from their hands.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Alfie, this is your share of the profit. It's less than we hoped for, but perhaps we could borrow some textbooks first, then think about getting you into a school later...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Jake, you lost your leg for our caravan. I swear I'll take care of you for the rest of your life...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Everyone, our funds are just enough to secure the investor entry permits for each of us.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: For what's next, we'll have to plan that out after we enter DisCity. And for now, let's get some sleep. We'll cross the border at sunrise.

Unlike Vautour Bleu, who had witnessed the commissioner's greed and arrogance, those who remained at the camp still held onto their fantasies. They encouraged one another, counting the DisCoins just issued like precious gems.

steps.speaker: Alfie
steps.content: I'll just start with a book then... The books in DisCity must be nice and cheap! Maybe I can even buy one, and when I'm done reading it, I'll buy a next one...
Soft murmurs wove dreams of a better life in DisCity. But soon, they shattered beneath the sudden boom of gunfire.

steps.speaker: Jake
steps.content: What's that? Someone fired a gun?! ...It's from DisCity!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Stay calm! Everyone stay calm! It's not aimed at us!

steps.speaker: Jake
steps.content: But DisCity... Isn't it supposed to be a safe zone? Do they have wars here too?
The question floored Vautour Bleu. Her knowledge of DisCity proved just as limited. Not until now, as she heard the gunfire, did she grasp the true meaning behind the commissioner's cryptic warning.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: No, it's not a war. Just a shootout between gangs. It'll be over soon. DisCity's FAC isn't to be trifled with. Everything will quiet down quickly. By the time we enter the city tomorrow, things will be good.
She desperately shielded their fragile dreams with hollow words of comfort, yet in their eyes, she saw it—the dreams already fell apart.
Now welcomed into DisCity as the FAC's "honored guest," Vautour Bleu notices how Syndicate has changed from total chaos like a decade ago.
Though traces of war can still be seen in the rebuilt district, it has at least become a place where people can lead normal lives.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Heh... You know what, when I first came here ten years ago, this place was overrun with gangs and guns.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Several of my companions were lured away by them and disappeared ever since. Others tried sneaking to Eastside along the Rust, but of course they got arrested.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Then there were those who were so disappointed by DisCity trying to return home, only to find their homeland already destroyed.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Yet I... I can't do nothing then. I couldn't stop any of it, couldn't save anyone.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: <size=26>...The DisCity dream. Heh, what's the good of living here?</size>

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Of course you wouldn't understand. People like you can't even imagine how many Hypercubes we've spent in mopping up Syndicate. West District would be even better if fewer opportunists with no sense of morals like you are slippin' in.
The FAC soldier's cold remarks faze Vautour Bleu not. She lets out an amused sigh, her expression showing nothing but casual indifference tinged with nostalgia, without a trace of shame.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Hypercubes, you say... Yeah, some can ride down the road, while others must risk their lives just to sneak through the mud. Some even drown in that... And that's not even a shortcut, that's just the only path left.
Her thoughts drift to the man who fled from their caravan. He must have collapsed right on DisCity's border. The DisCity dream may be no good, but he couldn't even afford the luxury of bethinking it.
Yet why does she still offer him a chance to dream? Even after Désir crumbled, even after the DisCity dream was proven false once again.
In a daze, Vautour Bleu glimpses a familiar silhouette through the vehicle's window. The figure that once appeared among datura flowers, behind the sheer curtains, and in sandy air.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We meet again, Miss Vautour Bleu.
